remediation_steps.step:
Back up the source file before making any edits.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/appsec-lab/utils.py /opt/vuln-labs/appsec-lab/utils.py.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Backing up the file ensures that you can restore the original state if the changes introduce any issues.

Replace the use of pickle.loads with json.loads to safely deserialize the session data.

Command:
    #EDIT_FILE
    {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/appsec-lab/utils.py",
     "old_text": "session_obj = pickle.loads(decoded)",
     "new_text": "import json\nsession_obj = json.loads(decoded)"}

Why: Using json.loads instead of pickle.loads mitigates the risk of arbitrary code execution by limiting the deserialization to JSON-compatible data types.

Verify that the vulnerable pattern is removed from the file.

Command:
    #VERIFY_ABSENT
    {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/appsec-lab/utils.py",
     "pattern": "pickle.loads"}

Why: Ensuring the absence of the vulnerable pattern confirms that the insecure deserialization method is no longer used.

Perform a syntax check to ensure the file is still valid Python code after the edit.

Command:
    python3 -m py_compile /opt/vuln-labs/appsec-lab/utils.py

Why: Running a syntax check helps catch any syntax errors introduced during the code modification.
